To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coregulatory complexes that assemble on DNA in response to nuclear receptor activation are dynamic, and their assembly is influenced by the chromatin structure.

the nuclear receptors and coregulators are involved in the control of gene transcription, that they can be recruited to the same or to different sites on the same gene to regulate transcription, and that their recruitment to DNA can be modulated by epigenetic factors.
the recruitment of corepressors and chromatin-remodeling factors can suppress steroid hormone action in the developing brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie sex differences in the brain, with a focus on how steroid hormone action is regulated at the level of DNA.
understanding the mechanisms by which steroid hormones regulate brain function and behavior.
the role of coregulatory factors in the regulation and repression of steroid hormone action during brain development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coregulatory matrix is the key determinant of the nuclear receptor-mediated gene expression.
coregulators are the key players in the regulation of nuclear receptors-mediated gene transcription in developing brain.
the corepressors are not the only repressors of gene transcription, nor are the coactivators the only activators of gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of steroid receptor-mediated gene transcription is a dynamic process that involves the recruitment of co-activators and co-repressors, and chromatin-remodeling factors to DNA.
the regulation of gene expression is a complex process involving the integration of multiple signals.
the recruitment of corepressor complexes on the steroid receptor response element is an important step in the regulation of the steroid hormone response in the developing brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the regulation of gene expression by nuclear receptors and coregulators is a complex process, and it is likely to involve the dynamic assembly of different combinations of coactivators and corepressors.
the recruitment of corepressors and chromatin-binding factors on DNA may be an integral component of the nuclear receptor-mediated repression of gene transcription.
corepressor and chromatin-binding factors are not simply repressors of gene transcription.
